 6     Conclusion and future plans
In this paper, we generalize the results of [6], where we find an interesting connection
between the number of cycles in the breakpoint graph Gr(π) for a signed permutation π ∈
Bn and the signed generalized commuting probability Prπ (G), which is a generalization
of the generalized commuting probability, which was defined in [6]. In contrast to the
results of [6], in the case of π ∈ Bn , the following changes occur:

    • For π ∈ Bn , the parity of n − s(π) + 1 is not necessarily even, it can be any
      integer;
    • If G is a non-ambivalent group, then s(π) = 2k induces two equivalence classes
      of Prπ (G), namely:

        – Pr2k (G) = Prπ (G) for a positive π ∈ Bn ;
        – Pr−2k (G) = Prπ (G) for a non-positive π ∈ Bn ,

      such that Pr2k (G) 6= Pr−2k (G);
    • If G has an odd order, then Prπ (G) = Pr−k (G) = |G|

      π ∈ Bn and every k ∈ N.
    • If G has an abelian 2-sylow subgroup, and G is a direct sum of its 2-sylow subgroup
